settings.name_in_paper: Functional sequential treatment allocation (anytime upper bounds)
unmapped: Arms are compared through a general functional T(F) of the outcome cdf (quantiles, inequality/welfare/poverty measures), not the mean; regret is sum_t [max_i T(F^i) - T(F^{pi_t})]
T satisfies a restricted Lipschitz condition |T(F)-T(G)| <= C ||F-G||_inf for F in a class D of cdfs on [a,b] (Assumption 2.2); the learner knows the constant C
Outcomes in a known interval [a,b]; arbitrary dependence across arms within a round
settings.definition_quote: We assume that~$a \leq Y_{i,t} \leq b$ ... we define the (cumulative) regret of a policy~$\pi$ at horizon~$n$ as R_n(\pi) = \sum_{t=1}^n [\max_{i} \mathsf{T}(F^i)- \mathsf{T}(F^{\pi_{n,t}(Z_{t-1}, G_t)})]

settings.name_in_paper: Functional sequential treatment allocation, explore-then-commit with known horizon
unmapped: Arms are compared through a general functional T(F) of the outcome cdf; regret is sum_t [max_i T(F^i) - T(F^{pi_t})]
T satisfies a restricted Lipschitz condition with constant C in sup-norm over a class D of cdfs on [a,b] (Assumption 2.2)

settings.name_in_paper: Functional sequential treatment allocation, two treatments (lower bound)
unmapped: Arms are compared through a general functional T(F) of the outcome cdf; regret is sum_t [max_i T(F^i) - T(F^{pi_t})]
Assumption 3.3: T satisfies Assumption 2.2 and D contains a line segment {J_tau = tau H_1 + (1-tau) H_2} on which T is not constant; supremum taken over cdfs in this segment

symbols.eta_etc: exploration constant eta in (0,1) of the explore-then-commit policy
symbols.c_l: positive constant depending on the functional along the line segment (not depending on n or the policy)

conditions: every explore-then-commit policy satisfying the exploration condition with eta in (0,1)
Assumption 3.3 (line segment in D on which T is non-constant)

source.label: thm:LBETC
source.quote: There exists a constant~$c_l > 0$, such that, for every explore-then-commit policy~$\pi$ that satisfies the exploration condition with~$\eta \in (0, 1)$, and for any randomization measure, it holds that \sup ... \E [R_n(\pi)] \geq \eta c_l n^{2/3} for every n \geq 2.

results.notes: Maximal expected functional regret (Theorem 3.4, part 1). Quantity 'other' because the regret targets a general functional rather than the mean.

symbols.eta_etc: exploration constant eta in (0,1) of the explore-then-commit policy
symbols.c_l: positive constant c_l(n^*) depending on n^* and the functional

conditions: explore-then-commit policies satisfying the exploration condition with eta in (0,1) and with exploration length n_1(n) <= n^* for all n

source.label: thm:LBETC
source.quote: For every~$n^* \in \N$ there exists a constant~$c_l = c_l(n^*)$, such that, for every explore-then-commit policy~$\pi$ that satisfies (i) the exploration condition with~$\eta \in (0,1)$ and (ii)~$n_1(\cdot)\leq n^*$ ... \geq \eta c_l n for every n \geq 2.

results.notes: Part 2: linear regret for ETC policies with bounded exploration length (e.g., horizon unknown).

symbols.C_T: Lipschitz constant C of the functional in Assumption 2.2

conditions: F^i in D for all i

source.label: thm:ETCES
source.quote: Under Assumptions~\ref{as:MAIN} and~\ref{as:MB}, the explore-then-commit empirical-success policy~$\tilde{\pi}$ satisfies \sup_{F^i \in \mathscr{D}} \E [R_n(\tilde{\pi})] \leq 6CKn^{2/3} for every n \in \N.

results.notes: Policy computational cost depends on evaluating the functional; not stated. Holds for every n.

symbols.C_T: Lipschitz constant C of the functional in Assumption 2.2

conditions: F^i in D for all i
tuning: beta > 2; beta = 2 + sqrt(2) gives c <= sqrt(11) C

source.label: RegretBound
source.quote: Under Assumptions~\ref{as:MAIN} and~\ref{as:MB}, the F-UCB policy~$\hat{\pi}$ satisfies \sup_{F^i \in \mathscr{D}}\E [R_n(\hat{\pi})]\leq c\sqrt{K n \overline{\log}(n)} for every n \in \N, where~$c=c(\beta,C) = C \sqrt{ 2 \beta + (\beta+2)/(\beta-2)}$.

results.notes: Anytime policy (does not use n). Uses C in the confidence width.

symbols.c_l: positive constant depending on the functional along the line segment

conditions: any policy (possibly using n) and any randomization measure

source.label: thm:LB_NoCov
source.quote: Suppose~$K = 2$ and that Assumption~\ref{as:NCONSTLINE} holds. Then there exists a constant $c_l > 0$, such that for any policy~$\pi$ and any randomization measure, it holds that \sup ... \E [R_n(\pi)] \geq c_ln^{1/2} for every n \in \N.

results.notes: Minimax lower bound over all policies.

symbols.C_T: Lipschitz constant C of the functional in Assumption 2.2
symbols.d_beta: d(beta) = (beta W_0(e/(4 beta)))^{1/2} / (1 - (4 beta W_0(e/(4 beta)))^{1/2 - 1/(2 W_0(e/(4 beta)))}), W_0 principal Lambert W

conditions: F^i in D for all i

source.label: RegretBoundfaMOSS
source.quote: Under Assumptions~\ref{as:MAIN} and~\ref{as:MB}, the F-aMOSS policy~$\check{\pi}$ satisfies \sup_{F^i \in \mathscr{D}}\E [R_n(\check{\pi})]\leq C (4.83 + 6.66 \times d(\beta) + \sqrt{2\beta})\sqrt{\pi} \sqrt{K n} for every n \in \N

results.notes: Anytime, matches the sqrt(n) lower bound. pi here is the constant pi.

symbols.C_T: Lipschitz constant C of the functional in Assumption 2.2
